stem:
Padma works out \(\dfrac{3}{4} \div \dfrac{2}{5}\).

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The divisor is what the dividend produces, so write \(\dfrac{2}{5} \div \dfrac{3}{4}\).
Treat division of fractions like commutative multiplication, so \(\dfrac{2}{5} \div \dfrac{3}{4}\) equals the original.

teacher.key_rationale: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c, so 3/4 ÷ 2/5 = 3/4 × 5/2. Multiplying by the divisor skips the reciprocal. Reversing dividend and divisor changes the value. Commutativity of multiplication does not make division order free.
